question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $53u + 12v = \text{gcd}(53,12).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}53 & = & \color{red}12\cdot 4 & + & \color{red}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}12 & = & \color{blue}5\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}2 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 5 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(12,53) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}5 &= \color{red} 53 - 12\cdot 4 \\[3pt] \color{blue}2 &= \color{blue} 12 - 5\cdot 2 \\[3pt] 1 &= 5 - 2\cdot 2. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 5-{\color{blue}2}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 5-{\color{blue}[12-5\cdot 2]}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}5}\cdot 5 - 12\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[53-12\cdot 4]}\cdot 5 - 12\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 53\cdot 5 - 12\cdot 22\\[4pt] &= 53 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5} + 12 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-22}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=5$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, \[u+v=5+(-22)=-17. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $69u + 30v = \text{gcd}(69,30).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}69 & = & \color{red}30\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}9 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}30 & = & \color{blue}9 \cdot 3 & + & \color{blue}3 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 9 & = & 3 \cdot 3 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(69,30) =3.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}9 &= \color{red} 69 - 30\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}3 &= \color{blue} 30 - 9\cdot 3. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 3 &= 30-{\color{red}9 \cdot 3} \\[3pt] &= 30-{\color{red}(69-30\cdot 2)\cdot 3} \\[3pt] &= 30\cdot 7 - 69\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 69 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-3}) + 30 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{7} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-3)+7=4. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $86u + 35v = \text{gcd}(86,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}86 & = & \color{red}35 \cdot 2 & + & \color{red}16 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}35 & = & \color{blue}16\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}3 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 16 & = & 3\cdot 5 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(86,35) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}16 &= \color{red}86 - 35\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}3 &= \color{blue} 35 - 16 \cdot 2 \\[3pt] 1 &= 16 - 3\cdot 5 . \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 16-{\color{blue}3}\cdot 5 \\[3pt] &= 16-{\color{blue} [35 - 16 \cdot 2]}\cdot 5 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}16}\cdot 11 - 35\cdot 5 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[86-35 \cdot 2]} \cdot 11 - 35\cdot 5 \\[3pt] &= 86 \cdot 11 - 35 \cdot 27 \\[3pt] &= 86 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{11} + 35 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-27}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=11$ and $v=-27.$

Finally, \[u+v=11+(-27)=-16. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $80u + 35v = \text{gcd}(80,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}80 & = & \color{red}35\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}10 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}35 & = & \color{blue}10\cdot 3 & + & \color{blue}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 10 & = & 5 \cdot 2 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(80,35) =5.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}10 &= \color{red} 80 - 35\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}5 &= \color{blue} 35 - 10\cdot 3. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 5 &= 35-{\color{red}10}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 35-{\color{red}[80-35\cdot 2]}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 35\cdot 7 - 80\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 80 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-3}) + 35 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{7} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-3)+7=4. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $71u + 29v = \text{gcd}(71,29).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}71 & = & \color{red}29 \cdot 2 & + & \color{red}13 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}29 & = & \color{blue}13\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}3 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 13 & = & 3\cdot 4 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(71,29) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}13 &= \color{red}71 - 29\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}3 &= \color{blue} 29 - 13 \cdot 2 \\[3pt] 1 &= 13 - 3\cdot 4 . \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 13-{\color{blue}3}\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= 13-{\color{blue} [29 - 13 \cdot 2]}\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}13}\cdot 9 - 29\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[71-29 \cdot 2]} \cdot 9- 29\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= 71 \cdot 9 - 29 \cdot 22 \\[3pt] &= 71 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{9} + 29 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-22}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, \[u+v=9+(-22)=-13. \]
